_comment: How the sessions table sorts, and what it opens on (#645).
The two clients had drifted on three columns and nobody noticed, because the
shared case lists built for #619 prove that the *rules* agree — the filter, the
grouping, the formatting — and not one of them says which key the table opens
on or in which direction. The browser opened on the session seen longest ago
while the terminal opened on the one seen a moment ago, and both token columns
ran backwards, with the header arrow claiming the opposite in all three cases.
`want` is the order of ids under the default direction, which is the one the
header renders as a down arrow. internal/tui/sort_shared_test.go and
test/js/dashboard.test.mjs read this file and must agree case for case.
Only the keys both clients sort by are here. `out` and `ctx` are columns the
browser can sort and the terminal cannot, so there is nothing to agree with;
they follow the same sense as the other numeric columns and the dashboard suite

cases.why: the session that just moved is the one worth the glance
the biggest consumer first, not the smallest
by the rank the daemon sent, most active first
a session under remote control first, then by recency
